faqs.a: Type or paste text and the hashes compute instantly. For files, switch to the File tab and choose a file up to 100 MB — it is read locally and never uploaded.
faqs.q: How do I hash text or a file?

faqs.a: SHA-256 is the safe default today. MD5 and SHA-1 are fast but cryptographically broken — fine for checksums, never for passwords or security.

MD5 and SHA-1 are implemented in pure TypeScript inside this page, so they work everywhere. SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 use the browser's WebCrypto API, which needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).
A hash function turns any input into a fixed-length fingerprint. Even a one-letter change produces a completely different digest, which is why hashes detect corruption and tampering.
faqs.q: What is a hash, in simple terms?

faqs.a: Yes. Pick a file and compare the SHA-256 shown here with the checksum on the download page. If they match exactly, the file arrived intact.
faqs.q: Can I verify a downloaded file's checksum?

faqs.a: Hashing is one-way: you cannot recover the original text from a digest. Short or common inputs can still be guessed by brute force, so never rely on a plain hash to hide secrets.
faqs.q: Can someone reverse a hash to see my text?

hash-generator.formula:
digest = Hash(UTF-8 bytes of input)

Output lengths (hex chars):
  MD5 = 32, SHA-1 = 40, SHA-256 = 64,
  SHA-384 = 96, SHA-512 = 128
howTo: Choose the Text tab for text or the File tab for a file.
Type your text, or pick a file up to 100 MB.
Tick the algorithms you want — all five are on by default.
Read each digest; hashes for text update as you type.
Copy any digest with its copy button.
keyFacts: A cryptographic hash maps arbitrary input to a fixed-size digest.
SHA-256 produces 64 hex characters; SHA-512 produces 128.
MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security but still fine for simple checksums.
The same input always produces the same digest — hashes are deterministic.
Files are hashed locally; nothing is ever uploaded to a server.

hash-generator.quickAnswer: A hash is a fixed-length fingerprint of data — the same input always gives the same digest, and any change gives a completely different one. Developers use hashes to verify downloads, detect corruption, and fingerprint content. This tool computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 for text or files, entirely in your browser.

hash-generator.workedExample:
Hash the text hello with all five algorithms.

MD5(hello)     = 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592
SHA-1(hello)   = aaf4c61ddcc5e8a2dabede0f3b482cd9aea9434d
SHA-256(hello) = 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824
SHA-384(hello) = 59e1748777448c69de6b800d7a33bbfb9ff1b463e44354c3553bcdb9c666fa90125a3c79f90397bdf5f6a13de828684f
SHA-512(hello) = 9b71d224bd62f3785d96d46ad3ea3d73319bfbc2890caadae2dff72519673ca72323c3d99ba5c11d7c7acc6e14b8c5da0c4663475c2e5c3adef46f73bcdec043

Change one letter — Hello with a capital H — and every digest changes completely. That avalanche effect is what makes hashes useful for integrity checks.
